content:
A church that meets the requirements of section 501(c)(3) is exempt from federal income tax without applying to the IRS. Contributions to a qualifying church are generally tax-deductible, subject to the rules that apply to each donor and gift.

You still have choices to make. You can file Form 1023 for your own determination letter, or, if your network holds a group exemption, ask to join it. This guide explains both routes, and why Form 1023-EZ is not one of them: churches are not eligible to use it.

---

## What 501(c)(3) Status Gives Your Church

Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code provides tax exemption for organizations organized and operated exclusively for religious, charitable, educational, or other specified purposes.

| Benefit | What to know |
|---------|--------------|
| Tax-deductible donations | Contributions to a qualifying church are generally deductible, subject to donor and gift requirements |
| Federal income tax exemption | Exemption applies to exempt activities; unrelated business income may still be taxable |
| State tax exemptions | Each state sets its own rules; federal status does not settle them |

---

## A Church Is Exempt Without Applying

[Publication 1828, Tax Guide for Churches & Religious Organizations](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1828.pdf) says that churches that meet section 501(c)(3) "are automatically considered tax exempt and are not required to apply for and obtain recognition of tax-exempt status from the IRS." Calling an organization a church does not by itself establish eligibility; the IRS considers its facts and circumstances.

Many churches file Form 1023 anyway, for a determination letter. Publication 1828 says this recognition "assures church leaders, members and contributors that the church is recognized as exempt and qualifies for related tax benefits." Common reasons:

- **Donors** — Larger contributors may want written proof before they give.
- **Grantors** — Some foundations check the IRS listing or ask for the letter.
- **Banks and vendors** — Some ask for the letter before they open an account or give a nonprofit price.
- **State exemptions** — Some state and local agencies ask for the letter. See [State Sales and Property Tax Exemptions](/wiki/administrative/legal/state-sales-and-property-tax-exemptions).

Ask each of them what they accept before you decide. A group exemption, described below, is another way to get IRS recognition.

---

## Churches Are Not Eligible for Form 1023-EZ

Churches are not eligible to use Form 1023-EZ, whatever their size, receipts or assets. The [Instructions for Form 1023-EZ](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1023ez) say: "If you are seeking recognition as a church, school, or hospital, you are not eligible to use Form 1023-EZ and should instead submit Form 1023 if you wish to obtain a determination letter from the IRS."

---

## Joining Your Network's Group Exemption

If your church plant belongs to a denomination, association or network, ask whether it holds a group exemption. Publication 1828 says: "If the parent holds a group ruling, then the IRS may already recognize the church as tax exempt." The current rules are in [Rev. Proc. 2026-8, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-04](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2026-04_IRB#REV-PROC-2026-8). It supersedes Rev. Proc. 80-27, which Publication 1828 still cites. The IRS lists related guidance on its [Group exemption resources](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/group-exemption-resources) page.

### What a group exemption is

A group exemption letter is "a letter issued by the IRS to a central organization recognizing the exemption from federal income tax on a group basis for subordinate organizations." It "relieves each subordinate organization included in a group exemption letter from filing its own application for recognition of exemption." Your church is the subordinate organization. Your network is the central organization.

### What the network does

The network must have your church under its "general supervision or control." For general supervision, the network each year "obtains, reviews, and retains information on the subordinate organization's finances, activities, and compliance with annual filing requirements," and educates you about "the requirements to maintain tax-exempt status." For a church, affiliation can rest on "the sharing of common religious bonds or convictions with the central organization."

### What joining involves

- **A governing document.** Each subordinate "must have a governing instrument," whether or not it is incorporated.
- **A uniform purpose statement.** Subordinates with the same purpose "must have a uniform purpose statement in their governing instruments." Ask your network for the text.
- **Your own EIN.** "A central organization, and each subordinate organization, must have its own EIN." See [Getting Your Church's EIN](/wiki/administrative/legal/getting-your-churchs-ein).
- **The network adds you.** Its yearly report to the IRS lists new subordinates and states that the network "has written authorization to include the subordinate organizations in the group exemption letter." A network that is itself a church or an association of churches "may, but is not required to," send that report, so ask how yours adds new churches.

### The written authorization you sign

Your church gives the network signed, written consent. Rev. Proc. 2026-8 says: "This authorization must be in writing, and it must be signed by an officer of the subordinate organization with personal knowledge of the facts and with authority to legally bind the subordinate organization." The authorization "must acknowledge that the central organization may remove the subordinate organization from the group exemption letter with or without cause."

### If you leave, or the network loses its exemption

Before the network removes your church, it must give you "at least 30 days' notice." The IRS can also terminate the whole letter, for example when the network's own exemption is "automatically revoked."

For a church, the tax-exempt status itself does not depend on the letter. Its status "will not be affected by such non-acceptance or non-issuance, termination, or removal." What you lose is the IRS recognition the letter gave you. You may then file your own Form 1023 or join another group exemption, but a church "is not required to do so."

<Callout type="insight">
  Before you leave a network, find out how your donors, bank and state agencies use the network's group exemption number. Plan how you will document your status after you leave.
</Callout>

### Questions to ask your network

- Does the network hold a group exemption, and what is its group exemption number?
- Does the group exemption letter cover subordinates under section 501(c)(3)?
- What authorization do we sign, who on our side signs it, and can we keep a copy?
- What uniform purpose statement must our governing document contain?
- What information do we report to the network each year, and by what date?
- When will the network add us, and how do we confirm that the IRS lists us?
- Do we still need our own EIN, and who obtains it?
- What happens to our status, and to the letter we show donors, if we leave or the network is removed?

---

## Filing Form 1023 on Your Own

If you want your own determination letter, prepare:

- [ ] Your organizing document and amendments, plus bylaws if adopted
- [ ] An Employer Identification Number (EIN)
- [ ] Financial information: if you have existed less than a year, projections for the current year and the next two years
- [ ] A narrative of your worship, teaching, outreach and other activities
- [ ] Schedule A, which every church completes

The [Instructions for Form 1023](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1023) say your organizing document "must limit your purposes to those described in section 501(c)(3)" and "must provide for the permanent dedication of your assets to a section 501(c)(3) purpose." File electronically through Pay.gov and pay the user fee there. [Rev. Proc. 2026-5, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-01](https://www.irs.gov/irb/2026-01_IRB#REV-PROC-2026-5) sets the fee for Form 1023 at $600.

<Callout type="important">
  As of November 1, 2026, the Form 1023 user fee is $600. Fees and processing times change. Confirm the current fee with the IRS before you file, and check the IRS [Where's my application for tax-exempt status?](https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/charitable-organizations/wheres-my-application-for-tax-exempt-status) page for processing times.
</Callout>

---

## After You Have Recognition

- [ ] Keep your determination letter, or your network's group exemption letter and proof that you are listed, in a permanent file
- [ ] Give copies to banks, major donors and grantors as needed
- [ ] Apply for state and local exemptions separately

Publication 1828 lists churches among the organizations "not required to file Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-N." Other filings can still apply, such as employment tax returns, or Form 990-T for unrelated business income.

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

**Choosing the streamlined form** — Churches are not eligible for Form 1023-EZ.

**Assuming you are covered** — Confirm that your network holds a group exemption and has added your church.

**Signing without reading** — The authorization lets the network remove you with or without cause.

**Missing required language** — Check the purpose and dissolution clauses before you file Form 1023.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
  *"Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s."* — Mark 12:17 (LSB)
</Callout>

Proper legal standing with the government allows your church to focus on its true mission—making disciples and glorifying God.
excerpt: How a church plant gets federal tax-exempt recognition: why churches are exempt without applying, why Form 1023-EZ is not for churches, filing Form 1023, and joining a network's group exemption under Rev. Proc. 2026-8.
title: Setting Up a 501(c)(3)

sources.claim: A church that meets section 501(c)(3) is exempt without applying.
sources.quote: Churches that meet the requirements of IRC Section 501(c)(3) are automatically considered tax exempt and are not required to apply for and obtain recognition of tax-exempt status from the IRS.

sources.claim: Many churches still seek recognition because it assures leaders, members and contributors; contributions are generally deductible.
sources.quote: Although there is no requirement to do so, many churches seek recognition of tax-exempt status from the IRS because this recognition assures church leaders, members and contributors that the church is recognized as exempt and qualifies for related tax benefits. For example, contributors to a church that has been recognized as tax exempt would know that their contributions generally are tax-deductible.

sources.claim: A church with a parent organization should ask whether the parent holds a group ruling.
sources.quote: If the parent holds a group ruling, then the IRS may already recognize the church as tax exempt.

sources.claim: Publication 1828 still cites Rev. Proc. 80-27 for group exemptions.
sources.quote: For general information on the group exemption process, see Publication 4573, Group Exemptions, and Revenue Procedure 80-27, 1980-1 C.B. 677.

sources.claim: Churches are not required to file Form 990, 990-EZ or 990-N.
sources.quote: The following is a list of some of the organizations that are not required to file Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-N. n Churches (as opposed to “religious organizations,” defined earlier)

sources.claim: Churches still have employment tax and unrelated business income filings.
sources.quote: Generally, churches and religious organizations are required to withhold, report and pay income and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA) taxes for their employees.

sources.claim: Form 990-T applies to unrelated business income.
sources.quote: If a church, or other exempt organization, has gross income of $1,000 or more for any taxable year from the conduct of any unrelated trade or business, it must file IRS Form 990-T

sources.claim: Churches are not eligible to use Form 1023-EZ.
sources.quote: If you are seeking recognition as a church, school, or hospital, you are not eligible to use Form 1023-EZ and should instead submit Form 1023 if you wish to obtain a determination letter from the IRS.

sources.claim: Churches may be considered exempt without filing Form 1023.
sources.quote: the following types of organizations may be considered tax exempt under section 501(c)(3) even if they do not file Form 1023 or Form 1023-EZ. Churches, including synagogues, temples, and mosques.

sources.claim: Organizations not required to apply may choose to file Form 1023 for a determination letter.
sources.quote: Even though these organizations aren't required to seek recognition of exemption, they may choose to file Form 1023 (or Form 1023-EZ, if eligible) to receive a determination letter stating they are recognized as exempt under section 501(c)(3) status.

sources.claim: Whether an organization is a church depends on its characteristics and facts and circumstances.
sources.quote: we will consider characteristics generally attributed to churches and the facts and circumstances of each organization applying for public charity classification as a “church.”

sources.claim: A church completes Schedule A.
sources.quote: IF you’re THEN you must complete Schedule A church A

sources.claim: The organizing document must limit purposes to section 501(c)(3) purposes.
sources.quote: Your organizing document must limit your purposes to those described in section 501(c)(3).

sources.claim: The organizing document must dedicate assets to a section 501(c)(3) purpose.
sources.quote: Your organizing document must provide for the permanent dedication of your assets to a section 501(c)(3) purpose.

sources.claim: An organization that has existed less than a year gives projections for the current year and the next two years.
sources.quote: If you’ve existed for less than 1 year, provide projections of your likely income and expenses for your current year and projections of your likely income and expenses for the next 2 years

sources.claim: Form 1023 is filed electronically through Pay.gov with the user fee.
sources.quote: You must pay this fee through Pay.gov when you file Form 1023.

sources.claim: The Form 1023 user fee is $600.
sources.quote: All other applications for recognition of exemption under § 501 except for those included in (1) of Appendix A of this revenue procedure and under § 521 (other than pension, profit-sharing, and stock bonus plans described in § 401). $600

sources.claim: Rev. Proc. 2026-8 supersedes Rev. Proc. 80-27.
sources.quote: This revenue procedure modifies and supersedes Rev. Proc. 80-27

sources.claim: What a group exemption letter is.
sources.quote: The term “group exemption letter” means a letter issued by the IRS to a central organization recognizing the exemption from federal income tax on a group basis for subordinate organizations described in § 501(c).

sources.claim: A group exemption relieves each subordinate from filing its own application.
sources.quote: This revenue procedure relieves each subordinate organization included in a group exemption letter from filing its own application for recognition of exemption.

sources.claim: The church must be under the network's general supervision or control.
sources.quote: Each subordinate organization initially included in a group application, or subsequently added to a group exemption letter, must be (1) affiliated with the central organization, and (2) subject to its general supervision or control

sources.claim: What the central organization does under general supervision.
sources.quote: Annually obtains, reviews, and retains information on the subordinate organization’s finances, activities, and compliance with annual filing requirements; and (ii) Annually transmits (including electronically) written information to, or otherwise educates, the subordinate organization about the requirements to maintain tax-exempt status

sources.claim: A church can show affiliation through common religious bonds.
sources.quote: in the case of a subordinate organization that is a church or a convention or association of churches, the sharing of common religious bonds or convictions with the central organization

sources.claim: A subordinate needs a governing instrument.
sources.quote: It must have a governing instrument (for example, a charter, trust indenture, articles of association, etc.), whether or not it is incorporated.

sources.claim: Subordinates with the same purpose need a uniform purpose statement.
sources.quote: Subordinate organizations that share the same purpose must have a uniform purpose statement in their governing instruments

sources.claim: Each subordinate needs its own EIN.
sources.quote: A central organization, and each subordinate organization, must have its own EIN.

sources.claim: The central organization reports added subordinates with a statement that it holds written authorization.
sources.quote: A statement that the central organization has written authorization to include the subordinate organizations in the group exemption letter

sources.claim: A church central organization need not submit the annual information.
sources.quote: A central organization described in § 501(c)(3) that is a church or a convention or association of churches and that maintains a group exemption letter may, but is not required to, submit the information described in this section 7.

sources.claim: The church plant gives the network signed written authorization.
sources.quote: A subordinate organization must authorize the central organization to include the subordinate organization in a group application or to add the subordinate organization to an existing group exemption letter. This authorization must be in writing, and it must be signed by an officer of the subordinate organization with personal knowledge of the facts and with authority to legally bind the subordinate organization.

sources.claim: The authorization acknowledges removal with or without cause.
sources.quote: The authorization described in this section 4.06 must acknowledge that the central organization may remove the subordinate organization from the group exemption letter with or without cause

sources.claim: The network gives at least 30 days' notice before removal.
sources.quote: A central organization must provide a subordinate organization with at least 30 days’ notice prior to removing the subordinate organization from the central organization’s group exemption letter.

sources.claim: The IRS may terminate the letter when the central organization's exemption is automatically revoked.
sources.quote: The central organization’s exemption is automatically revoked.

sources.claim: After removal the IRS no longer recognizes the subordinate unless it acts.
sources.quote: the IRS will not thereafter recognize the exemption of that subordinate organization unless such subordinate organization completes one of the actions described in section 9.05

sources.claim: A church's exempt status is not affected by termination or removal.
sources.quote: The tax-exempt status of any organization that is described in § 501(c)(3) that is a church or convention or association of churches and is (1) included as a subordinate organization in a group application that is not accepted or not issued, (2) part of a group exemption letter that is terminated, or (3) removed from a group exemption letter in accordance with section 8 of this revenue procedure, will not be affected by such non-acceptance or non-issuance, termination, or removal.

sources.claim: A church may file its own application or join another group exemption, but need not.
sources.quote: An organization (including a church or convention or association of churches) that is not required to apply for recognition of exemption under § 505 or § 508 and that has not had its exemption automatically revoked may obtain recognition of its exemption in the same manner described in section 9.05(2) of this revenue procedure, relating to procedures for an organization required to apply for recognition of exemption under § 505 or § 508, but the organization is not required to do so.

sources.claim: The IRS lists Rev. Proc. 2026-8 among its group exemption resources.
sources.quote: Published guidance Revenue Procedure 2026-8

sources.claim: A group exemption letter has the same effect as an individual letter.
sources.quote: A group exemption letter has the same effect as an individual exemption letter except that it applies to more than one organization.

sources.claim: The IRS publishes processing status for exemption applications.
